A rope horse that's inconsistent from one side isn't a training mystery — it's a physical one.

When Dr. Leo works a roping horse in North Texas, those one-sided patterns are almost always tied to restrictions in the mid-back and hindquarters. The horse isn't cheating. He's compensating.

Three things worth looking at before you pull your riggin' again:
— Is he dropping one shoulder in the box?
— Does he score clean one way and pull hard the other?
— Is he slow off the hind end on a specific side — consistently?

Those aren't training reps to drill out. Those are conversations your horse is having with you.

Dr. Leo is cAVCA-certified and works DFW and North Texas. If your partner's been inconsistent, let's talk.
